speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; please tell me, how many hours old were you when the symptoms first began?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

The history of prematurity (33 weeks) and onset of symptoms within two hours of birth is classic for RDS, likely due to surfactant deficiency. Given the gestational age and clinical presentation, a Chest_X-Ray would be the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes like pneumonia or transient tachypnea of the newborn (TTN).
